campaigns.title: Auto-detection finds the newest resumable run, whatever pipeline produced it

mutants.breaks: the query matches nothing, so `sw resume` reports 'No resumable runs found' while the failed run sits in flow_pipeline_runs — the exact shape of the defect this ticket fixed, and the one the old bundled-pipeline loop produced for every YAML-path run
a stale run outranks the one that just failed, which is what the bundled-list order did by accident and what 'the newest resumable one' was always supposed to prevent

mutants.old:
"WHERE project_name = ? AND status IN (?, ?, ?) "
                "ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1",
mutants.new:
"WHERE project_name = ? AND status NOT IN (?, ?, ?) "
                "ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1",
mutants.breaks: `sw resume` offers completed and running runs and refuses the parked ones, so resuming either restarts finished work or collides with a live run

mutants.old:
"SELECT * FROM flow_pipeline_runs "
                "WHERE project_name = ? AND status IN (?, ?, ?) "
mutants.new:
"SELECT * FROM flow_pipeline_runs "
                "WHERE project_name != ? AND status IN (?, ?, ?) "
mutants.breaks: resume picks up another project's run and executes its pipeline against this working tree — the one failure here that is a safety problem rather than an inconvenience

a resume re-runs every step that already passed — the persistence half of the journey, as opposed to the discovery half the other four mutants cover. Reported KILLED x1 here only because this campaign's scope is TECH-054's own two files; run against the whole suite it is killed by 14 tests across three tiers. Kept as the corpus's own record that resume-from-checkpoint is the well-protected half and auto-detection was the unprotected one

campaigns.title: Nothing writes over a command's documented output channel

mutants.breaks: the config DB writes its schema to stdout on every bootstrap, so `sw run --json` is unparseable from its first line — the state it shipped in, undetected, through a full green suite
every warning and error is interleaved into the command's own output, which is what a bare `RichHandler()` did for as long as the comment above it claimed stderr

`sw use` reports the switch and does not perform it once an active project already exists, so the next process still resolves the old one — the round-trip half of this journey, and invisible to any test that stays in one process
